title: Eulogy on Rainy Season
introduction: Rama eulogises the rainy season for a heavenly elixir is showered for all the living beings. This is one among the other eulogies to seasons. On this narration about rainy season, there are extensive commentaries by the ancient commentators as rainy season occupies a prime ordeal status among other seasons, and some of them are included here.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये किष्किन्ध काण्डे अष्ट विंशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 28th chapter in Kishkindha Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
स तदा वालिनम् हत्वा सुग्रीवम् अभिषिच्य च |
वसन् माल्यवतः पृष्टे रामो लक्ष्मणम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
sa tadā vālinam hatvā sugrīvam abhiṣicya ca |
vasan mālyavataḥ pṛṣṭe rāmo lakṣmaṇam abravīt
verses.translation: Rama spoke to Lakshmana while residing on the mountainside of Mt. Malayavata, also known as Mt. Prasavana, ensuing the elimination of Vali and enthronement of Sugreeva.

glosses.meaning: Mt. Malayavata - Prasavana, on upland of - mountainside

verses.devanagari:
अयम् स कालः संप्राप्तः समयो अद्य जल आगमः |
संपश्य त्वम् नभो मेघैः संवृतम् गिरि संनिभैः
verses.iast:
ayam sa kālaḥ samprāptaḥ samayo adya jala āgamaḥ |
sampaśya tvam nabho meghaiḥ saṃvṛtam giri saṃnibhaiḥ
verses.translation: "This is that time of which we thought and it has come to pass. Now it is rainy season. You see the sky fully covered with mountainous clouds.

glosses.meaning: that - time, of which we thought

verses.devanagari:
नव मास धृतम् गर्भम् भास्कारस्य गभस्तिभिः |
पीत्वा रसम् समुद्राणाम् द्यौः प्रसूते रसायनम्
verses.iast:
nava māsa dhṛtam garbham bhāskārasya gabhastibhiḥ |
pītvā rasam samudrāṇām dyauḥ prasūte rasāyanam
verses.translation: "Sustaining a nine-month pregnancy, impregnated through the Sun with his sunrays guzzling the essence of oceans, the heaven is giving birth to the elixir of life.
notes: The atmosphere bears pregnancy of rain water drawing through the sunrays, keeping that essence in air consolidating them to become watery clouds for a nine month period from the month of kārtīka to āṣāḍha. That is roughly from November to July. Then it delivers rainwater, the elixir of life, in the month of śrāvaṇa. It is an extract of six rasa-s elixirs, for the utilisation of various crops.

atra meghāḥ sūrya raśmi marut ādibhiḥ samudram udakam gṛhītvā garbhavt kārtīka māsa prabhṛti nava māsa dhṛtam sasyānām ṣaḍ rasa sampatti hetu bhūtam śuddham udakam śrāvaṇe māsi muncati it sūcitam -- dharmākūtam

glosses.meaning: of elixir [of life,] to the pregnancy

verses.devanagari:
शक्यम् अंबरम् आरुह्य मेघ सोपान पंक्तिभिः |
कुटज अर्जुन मालाभिः अलंकर्तुम् दिवाकरम्
verses.iast:
śakyam ambaram āruhya megha sopāna paṃk{}tibhiḥ |
kuṭaja arjuna mālābhiḥ alaṃkartum divākaram
verses.translation: "It is very likely to climb up the flight of stairs of clouds to bedeck the sun with the garlands of white wild-jasmines, and red Arjuna flowers, in these days.
notes: Vishnu or Narayana is located in the solar orb in the aspect of sun, calle sūrya nārayaṇa and he is to be adored in these days of rain before any bodily activity like eating or drinking is undertaken. dhyeyaḥ sadā savitṛ maṇḍala madhya vartī nārāyaṇam and this Vishnu is a 'decoration-happy' deity alankāra priyo viśṇuḥ and thus He can easily be reached by the stepladder formation of clouds and he can be garlanded easily. To do so a wife must be at his side sa patnyā viśālākśyā nārāyanam upāgamat 'adore that Narayana along with your wife...' and now if Rama were to adore that Supreme, Seetha is not at his side. Govindaraja.

glosses.meaning: to adorn, it is possible - in these days.

verses.devanagari:
संध्या राग उत्थितैः ताम्रैः अंतेषु अधिक पाण्डुरैः |
स्निग्धैः अभ्र पट च्छेदैः बद्ध व्रणम् इव अंबरम्
verses.iast:
saṃdhyā rāga utthitaiḥ tāmraiḥ aṃteṣu adhika pāṇḍuraiḥ |
snigdhaiḥ abhra paṭa cchedaiḥ baddha vraṇam iva ambaram
verses.translation: "Those clouds with pure white edges, and with reddish hue of sunset extending on them, look like soft pieces of cloth bandaged on the gashes of sky.
notes: The sky's parturition in the form of rain is just over and she is bandaged with cotton-like whitish and softish clouds, while the colour of spilt blood is still appearing on those dressings borrowed from the colour of sunset.

glosses.meaning: sunset time, with the hue of, extending - mottled with
at edges, much, whitish - pure white

verses.devanagari:
मन्द मारुत निःश्वासम् संध्या चंदन रंजितम् |
आपाण्डु जलदम् भाति काम आतुरम् इव अंबरम्
verses.iast:
manda māruta niḥśvāsam saṃdhyā caṃdana raṃjitam |
āpāṇḍu jaladam bhāti kāma āturam iva ambaram
verses.translation: "Slothful breezes as her sighs, sunset tingeing her as sandal paste, the sky with blanched clouds on her face appears like the one sighing for love.
notes: The birthing of rain is over and to give next birth to next rain, the sky is ready as a wooable female with sighs and daubing of sandal pastes to cool off her yearning for love.

glosses.meaning: slothful, breezes, out, breathing - as sighs
one with - love, longing, as if

verses.devanagari:
एषा घर्म परिक्लिष्टा नव वारि परिप्लुता |
सीता इव शोक संतप्ता मही बाष्पम् विमुंचति
verses.iast:
eṣā gharma parikliṣṭā nava vāri pariplutā |
sītā iva śoka santaptā mahī bāṣpam vimuṃcati
verses.translation: "Overly agonised with the searing-summer, but thoroughly wetted with new waters, this earth looks like Seetha, both implacably outpouring tears.
notes: The earth that becomes heated in summer vents out hot vapours on the fall of first rains releasing its agony of heat. The first act of humans to vent out agony is to shed tears. Now the earth is shedding humid tears and she is like Seetha who is also in the same predicament of earth, as the heat called the atrocity of Ravana sears Seetha.

glosses.meaning: by new, waters, thoroughly, flooded - wetted

verses.devanagari:
मेघ उदर विनिर्मुक्ताः कर्पूर दल शीतलाः |
शक्यम् अंजलिभिः पातुम् वाताः केतकि गन्धिनः
verses.iast:
megha udara vinirmuk{}tāḥ karpūra dala śītalāḥ |
śakyam aṃjalibhiḥ pātum vātāḥ ketaki gandhinaḥ
verses.translation: "Freed from the wombs of clouds, cool as the leaves of minty-camphor, perfumed with the fragrance of Mogra plants, such as these breezes are it is possible to have a draught of them with the bowl of palms.

glosses.meaning: from cloud's, womb, verily, out, freed [breezes
minty-camphor [yellow camphor,] [or, red-lotuses] leaves, with coolness of
Ketaki plant [Pandanus odora tissimus, Mogra,] with perfume of
with palms-bowl, to draught, possible to.

verses.devanagari:
एष फुल्ल अर्जुनः शैलः केतकैः अधिवासितः |
सुग्रीव इव शान्त अरिः धाराभिः अभिषिच्यते
verses.iast:
eṣa phulla arjunaḥ śailaḥ ketakaiḥ adhivāsitaḥ |
sugrīva iva śānta ariḥ dhārābhiḥ abhiṣicyate
verses.translation: "This mountain with fully bloomed Arjuna flowers, further fragranced by Ketaka flowers is being anointed with downpours on a par with Sugreeva, who is anointed when his enemy is silenced.
notes: This Mountain Prasavana is full with its blooming Arjuna flowers, like the colourful garlands on the chest of Sugreeva. It is further fragranced with Ketaka flowers, like the fragrant items brought for Sugreeva's anointment. As with Sugreeva who after silencing his enemy Vali is anointed on time with the pouring down of all kinds of waters from golden flasks, this is mountain after silencing its enemy called sun-sear, is also being anointed by rainy downpours.

glosses.meaning: fully bloomed, with Arjuna trees' flowers

verses.devanagari:
मेघ कृष्ण अजिन धरा धारा यज्ञ उपवीतिनः |
मारुत आपूरित गुहाः प्राधीता इव पर्वताः
verses.iast:
megha kṛṣṇa ajina dharā dhārā yajña upavītinaḥ |
māruta āpūrita guhāḥ prādhītā iva parvatāḥ
verses.translation: "Donning clouds as black deer skins, torrents as sacred-threads, and caves replete with breezes as vocals, the mountains look like young-scholars reciting Veda-s.
notes: The duty of young scholars of Vedic studies is to wear black deerskin and sacred thread as their initiation into Vedic studies. In these rainy days, there will be no other activity to them than sitting tight to recite their texts. The caves of mountains are its own mouths and they are replete with air and air gives out a din, and even the Vedic recitation gives out a din of its own kind. Thus, the mountains appear to be like humble young-scholars of Veda-s, voicing out their chanting like the hum of the air in caves.
atra parvatānām kṛṣṇa ajina yajñopavīta ādi dharma kalpena adhyetṛu sādṛśya pratipādanāt adhyetṛūṇām brahmacāriṇām kṛṣṇa ajina yajñopavīta ādi dhāraṇam dharma iti uktam - dk.

glosses.meaning: showers, ritual, mantled with - wearing sacred thread
well, studying - reciting ones [young-scholars,] are like.

verses.devanagari:
कशाभिः इव हैमीभिः विद्युद्भिः इव ताडितम् |
अन्तः स्तनित निर्घोषम् सवेदनम् इव अंबरम्
verses.iast:
kaśābhiḥ iva haimībhiḥ vidyudbhiḥ iva tāḍitam |
antaḥ stanita nirghoṣam savedanam iva ambaram
verses.translation: "While the flashes of lightning are whipping the sky as if they are the golden whips, it is letting out rattle of thunders holding out against its inly throes.

glosses.meaning: internally, with, throes, as though having - internally suffering with them.

verses.label: 4.28.12b
verses.devanagari:
नील मेघ आश्रिता विद्युत् स्फुरंती प्रतिभाति मे |
स्फुरंती रावणस्य अंके वैदेही इव तपस्विनी
verses.iast:
nīla megha āśritā vidyut sphuraṃtī pratibhāti me |
sphuraṃtī rāvaṇasya aṃke vaidehī iva tapasvinī
verses.translation: "That lightning hingeing on the blue cloud is squirmy, to me it appears like woeful Vaidehi squirming in the grasp of Ravana.

glosses.meaning: penitent - sorry state, Vaidehi, as if

verses.devanagari:
इमाः ता मन्मथवताम् हिताः प्रतिहता दिशः |
अनुलिप्ता इव घनैः नष्ट ग्रह निशा कराः
verses.iast:
imāḥ tā manmathavatām hitāḥ pratihatā diśaḥ |
anuliptā iva ghanaiḥ naṣṭa graha niśā karāḥ
verses.translation: "For those who are with their beloveds these precincts are advantageous, as their directions, as to which east and which is west, are unclear; and to loverless ones like me they are disadvantageous, because the same precincts have their planets and even their moon lost, and they look as though begrimed with dark-clouds.

glosses.meaning: for lovers having beloveds, [the precincts are] advantageous

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित् बाष्प अभिसंरुद्धान् वर्ष आगम समुत्सुकान् |
कुटजान् पश्य सौमित्रे पुष्टितान् गिरि सानुषु |
मम शोक अभिभूतस्य काम संदीपनान् स्थितान्
verses.iast:
kvacit bāṣpa abhisaṃruddhān varṣa āgama samutsukān |
kuṭajān paśya saumitre puṣṭitān giri sānuṣu |
mama śoka abhibhūtasya kāma saṃdīpanān sthitān
verses.translation: "Feeling happy with the arrival of rain wild jasmine plants standing somewhere on the terraces of mountain are flowered, and they are thickly covered with droplets of vapour, as if they are the tears of happiness hovering round the flower like faces of ladyloves at the arrival of their lovers, and such plants are becoming inciters of passion in me, who am let down by my sorrow for my ladylove.
notes: While some natural beings are enthused to take delight in the process of nature,brahma anubhava santuṣṭha, or Supreme Self, some others are refuting it. Thus my passion is increasing to bring back those perverts onto correct path.

glosses.meaning: of rainy season, by arrival of, feeling happy
my, sorrow, verily, one who is let down

verses.devanagari:
रजः प्रशांतम् स हिमो अद्य वायुः
निदाघ दोष प्रसराः प्रशांताः |
स्थिता हि यात्रा वसुधा अधिपानाम्
प्रवासिनो यांति नराः स्व देशान्
verses.iast:
rajaḥ praśāṃtam sa himo adya vāyuḥ
nidāgha doṣa prasarāḥ praśāṃtāḥ |
sthitā hi yātrā vasudhā adhipānām
pravāsino yāṃti narāḥ sva deśān
verses.translation: "In these days the dust is quietened, breeze is chilly, vile pervasions of summer are also quietened, conquests of kings indeed came to a halt, and the people in outstation are returning to their own countries.
notes: This verse speaks about the one who is blessed by the Supreme Being by way of His beneficence in the form of rain. For such a blessed soul rajaḥ which also means rajo guṇa, 'over-activism...' apart from the meaning of 'dust..' is silenced. This is one among the three attributes sattva, rajaḥ, tamo guṇā-s 'purity, activity, stolidity...' and thus rajaḥ praśāntam 'the quality of over-activity is quietened, along with the quality of stolidity...' thus, only 'purity' is evident in him in his worldly activities. sa himo vāyuḥ 'with, coldness, is air...' the word 'air' denotes 'breathing humans' and those blest human's heart breaths a cool breeze, rather than fumes and fires, that which is the attitude of a person who is dominated by rajo guna 'attribute of over-activity...' Thus, they the blessed souls have no evil effects of searing or scorching of summer. The compound nigadha doṣa... praśantāḥ means worldly affairs, are silenced, where vile of summer is the personified vile of worldly affairs. And even their worldly expeditions to conquer, to possess, and to become significant etc., are stalled for the blessed souls sthitāḥ... adhipānām. They have nothing to do here on earth because they are immigrants onto earth. So, they are returning to their own country, quarters, or abode, pravāsino... sva deśān. Their own place sva deśa is vaikunṭha. Thus the divine rain blesses them with salvation.

glosses.meaning: in outstation, those men who are, one's, own, to countries, they are going - returning.

verses.devanagari:
संप्रस्थिता मानस वास लुब्धाः
प्रिय अन्विताः संप्रति चक्रवाकः |
अभीक्ष्ण वर्ष उदक विक्षतेषु
यानानि मार्गेषु न संपतन्ति
verses.iast:
samprasthitā mānasa vāsa lubdhāḥ
priya anvitāḥ samprati cakravākaḥ |
abhīkṣṇa varṣa udaka vikṣateṣu
yānāni mārgeṣu na sampatanti
verses.translation: "Presently swans have started journey to Lake Manasa eager to live there, but the Cakravaka birds, ruddy gees, that are together with their beloveds are not departing, and vehicles are not taking to road as the rainwater has battered the roadways oftentimes.
notes: The swans do not like muddy waters so they aspire the clear waters of Lake Maanasa in Himalayas. The great sages, averse to muddy worldly affairs, are also called 'swans, supreme swans' hamsa, parama hamsa for they wander all over acquiring and disseminating spirituality to world. But they take break in rainy season in a vow called cātur māsyam and contemplate in their own manas 'mind' about the Supreme Being. If the swans tend to go to Himalayan Maanasa Lake, these sagely-swans tend to gain entry into their own mind in search of Supreme. And, like swans that can search and separate milk from water to drink milk alone, the sages can search for their being. The compound sam prasthitā, indicates a journey towards Supreme. And priya anvitā indicates involvement in worldly affairs, nominally indicated here as 'together with their lovers'. Contrarily, those ruddy gees bound by attachments do not flee away, but they will stick to their worldly interests. Thus, this rainy season is sagely, to enable the seekers to seek the Supreme, without any bickerings due from the world.

glosses.meaning: at Lake Maanasa, to live, eager to
Cakravaka [ruddy gees,] with beloved one, conjoined with
oftentimes, by rainy, waters, verily battered
not, verily, falling - not moving ahead.

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित् प्रकाशम् क्वचिद् अप्रकाशम्
नभः प्रकीर्णा अंबु धरम् विभाति |
क्वचित् क्वचित् पर्वत संनिरुद्धम्
रूपम् यथा शान्त महार्णवस्य
verses.iast:
kvacit prakāśam kvacid aprakāśam
nabhaḥ prakīrṇā ambu dharam vibhāti |
kvacit kvacit parvata saṃniruddham
rūpam yathā śānta mahārṇavasya
verses.translation: "Widely bestrewn with clouds the sky is bright somewhere, and not so bright somewhere else, thus it is gleaming well with an aspect of vast but tideless ocean that is by far dammed up with cloudlike mountains.
notes: The sky, or heaven, is also called Supreme Being, according to the saying kham brahma 'Sky is Brahman.' This is apparently shiny at places where the clouds of ignorance are not hovering on the minds of the discerners, and it is unshiny and unapparent at other places because of the gloom in the mind of the beholder about the disposition of that sky, or Supreme Being.

glosses.meaning: widely bestrewn with, water, carriers - clouds
somewhere, somewhere else - hear and there

verses.devanagari:
व्यामिश्रितम् सर्ज कदंब पुष्पैः
नवम् जलम् पर्वत धातु ताम्रम् |
मयूर केकाभिः अनुप्रयातम्
शैल अपगाः शीघ्रतरम् वहन्ति
verses.iast:
vyāmiśritam sarja kadamba puṣpaiḥ
navam jalam parvata dhātu tāmram |
mayūra kekābhiḥ anuprayātam
śaila apagāḥ śīghrataram vahanti
verses.translation: "Coalesced with Sarja and Wild-jasmine flowers, and also with the coppery ores of the mountain, the new waters are swiftly transiting towards ocean, while screams of peacocks haunting them.
notes: The flowers and mineral ores are mingling in waters and flowing as one with the waters. This is indicative of purposeful devotion, sātvika guṇa prathāna bhakti 'devotion in its pureness.' The sattva guṇa from the standpoint of mind is sukha 'devotion in pleasure....' and the rajo guṇa is 'pain...' thus that sort of devotion is rajo guṇa prathāna bhakti is 'devotion in pain...' Thus in pleasure or pain devoutness is evident. Apart from these two, there are some simple devotees. They do not have any higher values/purposes in view, except to extol, praise, and sing for the Ultimate. Thus, the screaming and screeching peacocks indicate such simple devotees. Govindaraja.

glosses.meaning: from mountains, water, goings - mountain rapids
swiftly, in higher degree, carrying away - flowing.

verses.devanagari:
रस आकुलम् षट्पद संनिकाशम्
प्रभुज्यते जंबु फलम् प्रकामम् |
अनेक वर्णम् पवन अवधूतम्
भूमौ पतति आम्र फलम् विपक्वम्
verses.iast:
rasa ākulam ṣaṭpada saṃnikāśam
prabhujyate jambu phalam prakāmam |
aneka varṇam pavana avadhūtam
bhūmau patati āmra phalam vipakvam
verses.translation: "The fruits of rose-apple that resemble honeybees are delightedly devoured as they are highly luscious, but the mango fruits that are discoloured and putrefied are falling to ground heaved down by wind.
notes: The falling of fruits on their own by the gusts of wind is indicative of the fall of fruits for a true devotee, and to him the ripened fruit is made available. Though Rose apple is an insignificant fruit it is consumed. It has a medicinal property in this rainy season. And though mango is a rich fruit it is not the season to consume it. So it is not picked now. Thus it is becoming a wasted fruit. Fruits of actions are therefore according to actions but not according to their richness or otherwise.

glosses.meaning: six, footed [honeybee,] nearly, equalling - that resemble
well, devoured aneka varNam = diversely, coloured - discoloured

verses.devanagari:
विद्युत् पताकाः स बलाक मालाः
शैलेन्द्र कूट आकृति संनिकाशाः |
गर्जन्ति मेघाः समुदीर्ण नादा
मत्त गजेन्द्रा इव संयुगस्थाः
verses.iast:
vidyut patākāḥ sa balāka mālāḥ
śailendra kūṭa ākṛti saṃnikāśāḥ |
gar.hjanti meghāḥ samudīrṇa nādā
matta gajendrā iva saṃyugasthāḥ
verses.translation: "Electric-charges as their fluttering flags of war, flights of cranes as their garlands of gallantry, those clouds very similar in their build to the pinnacles of lordly mountains are thundering with very high pitched voices like invigorated lordly elephants standing up to a fight.
notes: The towering mountains, or the haughty elephants stand tall among all, and their thunderous grumblings are akin to the rumblings of Vedic scholars who stand tall to establish Vedic tenets, though they come to fistfights with opponents.

glosses.itrans: shaila indra kuuTa aakR^iti sam nikaashaaH
glosses.iast: śaila indra kūṭa ākṛti sam nikāśāḥ
glosses.devanagari: शैल इन्द्र कूट आकृति सं निकाशाः
glosses.meaning: mountain, lordly, pinnacles, in build, very, similar to
in a fight, standing up to

verses.devanagari:
वर्ष उदक आअप्यायित शाद्वलानि
प्रवृत्त नृत्त उत्सव बर्हिणानि |
वनानि निर्वृष्ट बलाहकानि
पश्य अपराह्णेषु अधिकम् विभान्ति
verses.iast:
varṣa udaka āapyāyita śādvalāni
pravṛtta nṛtta utsava barhiṇāni |
vanāni nirvṛṣṭa balāhakāni
paśya aparāhṇeṣu adhikam vibhānti
verses.translation: "When clouds have completely rained on the greenery pasturelands are satiated with rainwater and peacocks are stimulated to dancing carnivals, thus it is extremely splendorous in afternoons, behold it.
notes: The Divine couple Lakshmi and Narayana have grown this garden called earth, watering each of its plant with their Divine hands. Thus, due to the divine beneficence of that couple in the form of rain, that which is sprinkled on that garden, the desires of living beings and their means are fulfilled. Govindaraja. The aparāhṇa is the fourth part of daytime, among the five, and they are: prātaḥ, sangavaḥ, madhyāhna, aparāhṇa, sāyāhnaearly morning, morning, noon, afternoon, and evening.

glosses.meaning: stimulated, for dance, carnivals, of peacocks

verses.devanagari:
सम् उद् वहन्तः सलिल अति भारम्
बलाकिनो वारि धरा नदन्तः |
महत्सु शृंगेषु मही धराणाम्
विश्रम्य विश्रम्य पुनः प्रयान्ति
verses.iast:
sam ud vahantaḥ salila ati bhāram
balākino vāri dharā nadantaḥ |
mahatsu śṛṃgeṣu mahī dharāṇām
viśramya viśramya punaḥ prayānti
verses.translation: "Clouds adorned with cranes around them are rumbling to transport them, and the weighty water contained inside their wombs, and reposing on the loftiest mountain peaks they are moving, moving and again reposing, like pregnant women.
notes: The saintly persons and pregnant mothers are indicated by these clouds. hṛdayena ud vahan harim 'The Supreme is to be carried along by one's own heart...' thus with their complete knowledge about that Supreme the saintly persons are repeatedly reposing at a sinful situation, and proceeding further when that sin is absolved. Thus they journey further towards total salvation. A pregnant woman also moves haltingly like a cloud carrying water. The clouds are pregnant not only by the weighty water but also by carrying the weight of cranes. The cranes fly high up to the clouds to mate. Thus, the clouds are loaded down with their own water and even with the flying cranes, both trying to carry the seed, the Supreme Being, in their wombs.

glosses.meaning: with water, much, weighty - contained inside the wombs of clouds
by earth, born ones - of mountains

verses.devanagari:
मेघ अभिकामा परिसंपतन्ती
सम्मोदिता भाति बलाक पंक्तिः |
वात अवधूता वर पौण्डरीकी
लंब इव माला रुचिर अंबरस्य
verses.iast:
megha abhikāmā parisampatantī
sammoditā bhāti balāka paṃk{}tiḥ |
vāta avadhūtā vara pauṇḍarīkī
lamba iva mālā rucira ambarasya
verses.translation: "Highly delighted cranes are flying all over in rows highly desirous of the clouds, and they are shining forth like the best and lovely festoons of white lotus flowers as if wind has upheaved and dangled them on the sky.
notes: The white flying cranes desire black clouds for their mating. It indicates that the pure white conscious is desiring the Supreme abiding beyond the dark/obscured quarters and thus this pure white conscious of the true devotee is flying up above the normal planes to merge into that unknown, dark, or obscured zone to have a glimpse of that Supreme, whose body colour is said to be 'blue' or 'blue-black' kāla megha śyāma, nīla megha śyāma like that of the colourless sky.

glosses.meaning: above, well, falling - flying all over

verses.devanagari:
बाल इन्द्रगोप्ता अंतर चित्रितेन
विभाति भूमिः नव शाद्वलेन |
गात्र अनुपृक्तेन शुक प्रभेण
नारी इव लाक्ष उक्षित कंबलेन
verses.iast:
bāla indragoptā aṃtara citritena
vibhāti bhūmiḥ nava śādvalena |
gātra anupṛk{}tena śuka prabheṇa
nārī iva lākśa ukśita kambalena
verses.translation: "The meadowland is with its new meadows which are medially dappled with young and small red-beetles, and it is shining forth as if she is a woman wearing a parrot-green wraparound on which lac-red spots are embroidered.
notes: It is usual for the insects to swarm on the new pasturelands by which the earth is appearing to be wearing a parrot-green colour sari embroidered with exotic red spots. The red colour is indicative of mercy of Supreme Being appearing opportunely, and the green pastures are His fertile kindness that reveal after humanly suffering, say summer heat.

glosses.meaning: lac-red, besprinkled - embroidered, with shawl - with wraparound

verses.devanagari:
निद्रा शनैः केशवम् अभ्युपैति
द्रुतम् नदी सागरम् अभ्युपैति |
हृष्टा बलाका घनम् अभ्युपैति
कान्ता स कामा प्रियम् अभ्युपैति
verses.iast:
nidrā śanaiḥ keśavam abhyupaiti
drutam nadī sāgaram abhyupaiti |
hṛṣṭā balākā ghanam abhyupaiti
kāntā sa kāmā priyam abhyupaiti
verses.translation: "These days sleep is slowly getting closer to Vishnu, rivers are rapidly getting closer to oceans, cranes are gleefully getting closer to clouds, and women are passionately getting closer to their beloveds.
notes: Vishnu goes into yogic trance from āṣāḍha ekādaśī to kārtīka śuddha ekādaśi thus He concentrates on the sustenance of the Universe, as an expression of His satisfaction līla. He is śeśin 'lord' and all other beings are śeśa 'servants.' Thus, all the servants are eager to get in touch with the master. Govindaraja. Dharmaakuutam put this as: atra caturṣvapi pādeṣu nidrā nadī balākā kāntānām sva sva priyatān keśava samudra ghana patīnān prati svata eva abhisaraṇa kathanāt patim pratyabhisaraṇaśīlā abhisārikā sūcitam - - varṣā kāle strīṇām kāmodreka uktaḥ -- balākānām garbha dhāraṇārtham sajalam ghanam prati gamamanam uktam -- dk Further he quotes from Kalidasa's megha sandeśa :garbhādhān kṣaṇa paricayān nūnam ābaddha mālāḥ | sevante nayana subhagam khe bhavantam balākāḥ || meghasandeśa.

atra caturṣvapi pādeṣu nidrā nadī balākā kāntānām sva sva priyatān keśava samudra ghana patīnān prati svata eva abhisaraṇa kathanāt patim pratyabhisaraṇaśīlā abhisārikā sūcitam - - varṣā kāle strīṇām kāmodreka uktaḥ -- balākānām garbha dhāraṇārtham sajalam ghanam prati gamamanam uktam -- dk
Further he quotes from Kalidasa's megha sandeśa :
garbhādhān kṣaṇa paricayān nūnam ābaddha mālāḥ | sevante nayana subhagam khe bhavantam balākāḥ || meghasandeśa.

glosses.meaning: sleep, slowly, to Keshava [Vishnu,] closely, getting at
river, rapidly, to ocean, closer, getting at
gleefully, female crane, to cloud, closely, getting at
with, passion, woman, to beloved, closely, getting at.

verses.devanagari:
जाता वनान्ताः शिखि सुप्रनृत्ता
जाताः कदंबाः स कदंब शाखाः |
जाता वृषा गोषु समान कामा
जाता मही सस्य वन अभिरामा
verses.iast:
jātā vanāntāḥ śikhi supranṛttā
jātāḥ kadambāḥ sa kadamba śākhāḥ |
jātā vṛṣā goṣu samāna kāmā
jātā mahī sasya vana abhirāmā
verses.translation: "Interiors of forests have become adaptive for the peacocks to dance very well, Kadamba trees have become adaptive to their branches and bouquets, bulls with matching sensualities became adaptive to cows, and adaptive is this earth with its enrapturing crops and orchards, and all are adaptive to the season's gaiety.

glosses.meaning: for peacocks, very, well, to dance
bulls, in cows, matching, in sensualities, adaptive

verses.devanagari:
वहन्ति वर्षन्ति नदन्ति भान्ति
ध्यायन्ति नृत्यन्ति समाश्वसन्ति |
नद्यो घना मत्त गजा वन अन्ताः
प्रिया विहीनाः शिखिनः प्लवंगाः
verses.iast:
vahanti var.hṣanti nadanti bhānti
dhyāyanti nṛtyanti samāśvasanti |
nadyo ghanā matta gajā vana antāḥ
priyā vihīnāḥ śikhinaḥ plavaṅgāḥ
verses.translation: "Rivers are surging, clouds are showering, rutty elephants are shrilling, forest interiors are shining, loverless are speculating, and peacocks are rocking, monkeys are resolving to stay at one place, for this is the rainy season.
notes: The monkeys have resolved to stay at one place without hopping hither and thither as the fruits for them are abundant at any one place.

verses.devanagari:
प्रहर्षिताः केतक पुष्प गन्धम्
आघ्राय मत्ता वन निर्झरेषु |
प्रपात शब्द आकुलिता गजेन्द्राः
सार्धम् मयूरैः स मदा नदन्ति
verses.iast:
praharṣitāḥ ketaka puṣpa gandham
āghrāya mattā vana nir.hjhareṣu |
prapāta śabda ākulitā gajendrāḥ
sārdham mayūraiḥ sa madā nadanti
verses.translation: "On whiffing the fragrance of new Ketaka flowers the lordly elephants are highly joyous and became excited, but they are baffled at the sounds made by the fall of water in the streamlets of forest, and those best ruttish elephants are blaring along with screaming peacocks.
notes: The elephants are confused at the sounds of mountain rapids falling to form brooklets in the forest and they construe those sounds are from an attacking elephant, thus they are giving out their challenge trumpeting. The peacocks are also screaming at the same sounds of rapids thinking them to be rainfall, as they welcome the rainfall to start dancing in the rain.

verses.devanagari:
धारा निपातैः अभिहन्यमानाः
कदंब शाखासु विलंबमानाः |
क्षण अर्जितम् पुष्प रस अवगाढम्
शनैर् मदम् षट् चरणाः त्यजन्ति
verses.iast:
dhārā nipātaiḥ abhihanyamānāḥ
kadamba śākhāsu vilambamānāḥ |
kṣaṇa arjitam puṣpa rasa avagāḍham
śanair madam ṣaṭ caraṇāḥ tyajanti
verses.translation: "Honeybees languishing on the branches of Kadamba trees are knocked down by the downpour of rain, thereby they are slowly forfeiting the intemperance which they acquired in a trice by plunging themselves into the nectar of flowers.

glosses.meaning: streams, by falling down - by downpours of rain
in a moment, acquired - which is acquired in a trice

verses.devanagari:
अंगार चूर्ण उत्कर संनिकाशैः
फलैः सुपर्याप्त रसैः समृद्धैः |
जंबू द्रुमाणाम् प्रविभान्ति शाखा
निपीयमाना इव षट्पद ओघैः
verses.iast:
aṃgāra cūrṇa utkara saṃnikāśaiḥ
phalaiḥ suparyāpta rasaiḥ samṛddhaiḥ |
jambū drumāṇām pravibhānti śākhā
nipīyamānā iva ṣaṭpada oghaiḥ
verses.translation: "Rose-apple trees contain abundant fruits with profuse juice which look like the globated coal powder, with them the branches of those trees shine forth as though swilled by hives of honeybees.

glosses.meaning: coal, powder, heap [globes,] equalling in aspect
by honeybees, multitude of - hives of

verses.devanagari:
तडित् पताकाभिः अलंकृतानाम्
उदीर्ण गंभीर महा रवाणाम् |
विभान्ति रूपाणि बलाहकानाम्
रण उत्सुकानाम् इव वारणानाम्
verses.iast:
taḍit patākābhiḥ alaṃkṛtānām
udīrṇa gambhīra mahā ravāṇām |
vibhānti rūpāṇi balāhakānām
raṇa utsukānām iva vāraṇānām
verses.translation: "Ornamented with the flags of lightning, and that have whooping, profound and blaring booms, those clouds by their appearances are verily shining forth like the elephants enthusiastic for a war.

glosses.meaning: having whooping, profound, great, having sounds - booms

verses.devanagari:
मार्ग अनुगः शैल वन अनुसारी
संप्रस्थितो मेघ रवम् निशम्य |
युद्ध अभिकामः प्रतिनाद शन्की
मत्तो गजेन्द्रः प्रतिसंनिवृत्तः
verses.iast:
mārga anugaḥ śaila vana anusārī
samprasthito megha ravam niśamya |
yuddha abhikāmaḥ pratināda śankī
matto gajendraḥ pratisaṃnivṛttaḥ
verses.translation: "That energetic and lordly elephant which readily started going towards the forest minding the track of that mountain, heard the thundering of the cloud, and doubting it a the war-whoop of another elephant took a right about turn wishing for a head-on collision with it.
notes: The 'warring elephant' is indicative of Vedic proponent, where any such scholar on hearing the profound and uproarious challenge of his opponent, he will re-echo the same in order to retain his stand in the war of blaring words. Thus, he takes an elephantine U-turn to colloid headlong with his opponent to establish the Vedic dharma.

glosses.meaning: return, shout [challenge of another elephant,] doubting
for a fight, interested towards - for a head-on collison
mountain, way, follower - minding the track of mountain

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित् प्रगीता इव षट्पद ओघैः
क्वचित् प्रवृत्ता इव नील कण्ठैः |
क्वचित् प्रमत्ता इव वारण इन्द्रैः
विभाति अनेक आश्रयिणो वनान्ता
verses.iast:
kvacit pragītā iva ṣaṭpada oghaiḥ
kvacit pravṛttā iva nīla kaṇṭhaiḥ |
kvacit pramattā iva vāraṇa indraiḥ
vibhāti aneka āśrayiṇo vanāntā
verses.translation: "Somewhere the interiors of forests are finely singing, in affect, as they have swarms of singing honeybees; elsewhere, they are richly dancing, practically, as the purple-necked peacocks are bestirring; somewhere else, they are highly excited, virtually, as lordly elephants are highly excited, thus the interiors of forests are beaming forth as retreats to many bees, birds and animals.

glosses.meaning: to many, a retreat - to birds, animals etc

glosses.itrans: kvachit SaTpada oghaiH pra giitaa iva
glosses.iast: kvacit ṣaṭpada oghaiḥ pra gītā iva
glosses.devanagari: क्वचित् षट्पद ओघैः प्र गीता इव
glosses.meaning: = somewhere, with hexapods - honeybees, by swarms of, well, sung, as if

glosses.itrans: kvacit niila kaNThaiH pra vR^ittaa iva
glosses.iast: kvacit nīla kaṇṭhaiḥ pra vṛttā iva
glosses.devanagari: क्वचित् नील कण्ठैः प्र वृत्ता इव
glosses.meaning: elsewhere, purple colour, necked ones - peacocks, pleasantly, bestirring [well danced,] as if

glosses.itrans: kvacit vaaraNa indraiH pra mattaa iva
glosses.iast: kvacit vāraṇa indraiḥ pra mattā iva
glosses.devanagari: क्वचित् वारण इन्द्रैः प्र मत्ता इव
glosses.meaning: somewhere else, with elephants, lordly, highly, excited, as if

verses.devanagari:
कदंब सर्जा अर्जुन कंदल आढ्या
वनान्त भूमि मधु वारि पूर्णा |
मयूर मत्ता अभिरुत प्रवृत्तैः
अपान भूमि प्रतिमा विभाति
verses.iast:
kadamba sarjā arjuna kaṃdala āḍhyā
vanānta bhūmi madhu vāri pūrṇā |
mayūra mattā abhiruta pravṛttaiḥ
apāna bhūmi pratimā vibhāti
verses.translation: "Plentiful in Kadamba, Sarja, Arjuna, Kandala trees and with the heaps of their reddish flowers fallen on ground, and well-excited peacocks screaming and dancing like the tipplers of that liquor like nectar, thus the interiors of forest are aplenty with nectar of those fallen flowers flowing like water, thus they are impressively similar to the lands of liquor, say watering-holes.
notes: The ancient Indian liquor lounges are rather open spaces with palm/toddy trees in and around. The boozers used to wear flowery garlands and flowery armlets and they used to drink in the pinkish buds of banana flowers, which served mostly like the present day 'use and throw' plastic mugs. The screaming and dancing of nectar-drunk peacocks is metaphoric with the liquor-drunk boozers, or, say cabaret artists, and the land itself is boozy.

glosses.meaning: with Kadamba, Sarja, Arjuna, Kandala trees, plentiful in
with peacocks, excited, well, by screaming, by stirring up [dancing]

verses.devanagari:
मुक्ता समाभम् सलिलम् पतत् वै
सुनिर्मलम् पत्र पुटेषु लग्नम् |
हृष्टा विवर्ण च्छदना विहंगाः
सुरेन्द्र दत्तम् तृषिताः पिबन्ति
verses.iast:
muk{}tā samābham salilam patat vai
sunirmalam patra puṭeṣu lagnam |
hṛṣṭā vivarṇa cchadanā vihaṃgāḥ
surendra dattam tṛṣitāḥ pibanti
verses.translation: "Extremely clear, pure, pearl-similar rainwater given as a gift by Indra is falling down and clinching the hallows of leaves, such as it is, it is heartily guzzled down by the thirsty birds whose wings are discoloured by the same water.
notes: Indra is the administrative authority to accord rain through the presiding deity of Rain, namely varuNa, the Rain-God. So also, all the other aspects of nature like air, fire, thunders, thunderbolts, crops, famines, earthquakes, and the whole of natural happenings are at Indra's behest.

glosses.meaning: gods, king - Indra, given - gift of
verily - pure, without, dirt - extremely clear

verses.devanagari:
षत्पद तंत्री मधुर अभिधानम्
प्लवंगम् उदीरित कण्ठ तालम् |
आविष्कृतम् मेघ मृदंग नादैः
वनेषु संगीतम् इव प्रवृत्तम्
verses.iast:
ṣatpada taṃtrī madhura abhidhānam
plavaṃgam udīrita kaṇṭha tālam |
āviṣkṛtam megha mṛdaṃga nādaiḥ
vaneṣu saṃgītam iva pravṛttam
verses.translation: "Melodious string bass of honeybees as stringendo, frogs crocking as vocal rhythm, fortissimos of clouds as drumbeats, music has commenced in the forest as though programmed.
notes: On this and next verses that contain the aspect of 'Nature's Music' dharmākūtam records extensive commentary with reference to the 'Art of Music' sangīta śāstra Here only three instruments, namely sting instrument vīṇa percussion instrument mṛidañga and vocalised rhythm beat tāla are suggested. But these do not exclude the other components of music. The commentator says that the dancing and singing are also inclusive of it, as contained in the next verse: atra vīṇā tāla mṛdañga vādya mātram pratipādya sangītam pravrittam iti uktvā vakṣyamānam nṛtta gīta api abhipretam - gītam vādyam tathā nṛtyam trayaḥ sangītam uccyate -- śārañga deva...Then the commentator proceeds to say that whole of the epic is replete with music for it is rendered as singable poetry:
tathā ca bhagavatā vālmīki maharṣiṇā svasya parama puruṣa rūpa abhidhyāna artham gīti rūpam rāma caritam varṇitam | gāna arthatayā rāma nikaṭe kuśa lavayoḥ preṣaṇam tu.

glosses.meaning: music, programmed, as though - the environs filled with such music.

verses.devanagari:
क्वचित् प्रनृत्तैः क्वचित् उन् नदद्भिः
क्वचित् च वृक्ष अग्र निषण्ण कायैः |
व्यालंब बर्ह आभरणैः मयूरैः
वनेषु संगितम् इव प्रवृत्तम्
verses.iast:
kvacit pranṛttaiḥ kvacit un nadadbhiḥ
kvacit ca vṛkśa agra niṣaṇṇa kāyaiḥ |
vyālamba barha ābharaṇaiḥ mayūraiḥ
vaneṣu saṃgitam iva pravṛttam
verses.translation: "Somewhere dancing well, elsewhere voicing in high pitch, and somewhere else seated high on the trees are the peacocks with plumaged tails as their dangling decorations, and it appears as the music and dance have commenced in the forests as programmed.
notes: The dancing peacocks are the dancers, the voicing peacocks around the dancing peacocks are the singers and instrumentalists, and the peacocks that are sitting atop trees dangling their tails and conducting the ballet are the virtuosos / maestros: atra nṛtyanto mayūrā nartakā iva bhavanti | unnadanto mayūrāḥ gāyakā vādakā iva ca bhavanti | ucca sthāna sthita sabhā nāyakā iva bhavanti | dk.

glosses.meaning: somewhere, those that are dancing well

glosses.itrans: kvacit vR^iksha agra niSaNNa kaayaiH ca
glosses.iast: kvacit vṛkśa agra niṣaṇṇa kāyaiḥ ca
glosses.devanagari: क्वचित् वृक्श अग्र निषण्ण कायैः च
glosses.meaning: somewhere else, of tree, on high, seated, with bodies, also
in forest, music [and dance,] commenced, as though.

verses.devanagari:
स्वनैः घनानाम् प्लवगाः प्रबुद्धा
विहाय निद्राम् चिर संनिरुद्धाम् |
अनेक रूपा आकृति वर्ण नादा
नव अंबु धारा अभिहता नदन्ति
verses.iast:
svanaiḥ ghanānām plavagāḥ prabuddhā
vihāya nidrām cira saṃniruddhām |
aneka rūpā ākṛti varṇa nādā
nava ambu dhārā abhihatā nadanti
verses.translation: "Thunders of clouds called up the frogs, and casting off their long-time captivity in sleep, frogs of various casts, carves, colours and crocks are crocking scourged heavily by the streams of new waters.
notes: Frogs are the foretellers of rain and they quickly respond to the rainfall because they cherish water and land alike, as amphibians, for their happy dwelling.

glosses.meaning: of various, cast, carve, colour, with crocks
by new, water, streams, verily, scourged

verses.label: 4.28.39b
verses.devanagari:
नद्यः समुद्वाहित चक्रवाका
तटानि शीर्णानि अपवाहयित्वा |
दृप्ता नव प्राभृत पूर्ण भोगा
द्रुतम् स्व भर्तारम् उपोप यान्ति
verses.iast:
nadyaḥ samudvāhita cakravākā
taṭāni śīr.hṇāni apavāhayitvā |
dṛptā nava prābhṛta pūrṇa bhogā
drutam sva bhartāram upopa yānti
verses.translation: "Prideful rivers are swiftly surging near and near of their lover-like ocean overflowing their own battered riverbanks, and in doing so they are swinging and seesawing flights of ruddy gees flying on their bosom, where the curvatures of bird-flight look like the new, full-fledged, seducible, nubile breasts of the river, and in doing so the river is also lugging other items of romance, namely flowers and fruits, steeped in their new waters.
notes: The rivers are the nubile girls and the over flying pairs/flights of Cakravaka birds are their heaving breasts. These girls called rivers are rushing towards their beloveds carrying flowers and fragrances etc., and they look like those girls that rush heaving their new breasts, uncaring for the elders of the house, or others in society around them, as though their lust is overflowing the brims of riverbanks, called the society.

glosses.meaning: well, up, hauled, Cakravaka - river water is sweeping ruddy gees up and along with its course - seesawing
new, well, lugging, full-fledged, seducible - nubile limbs, pair of breasts, and other fruits and flowers used in meeting lovers, now immersed in the river waters
swiftly, to his near, to his near, surging.

verses.devanagari:
नीलेषु नीला नव वारि पूर्णा
मेघेषु मेघाः प्रविभान्ति सक्ताः |
दवाग्नि दग्धेषु दवाग्नि दग्धाः
शैलेषु शैला इव बद्ध मूलाः
verses.iast:
nīleṣu nīlā nava vāri pūrṇā
megheṣu meghāḥ pravibhānti sak{}tāḥ |
davāgni dagdheṣu davāgni dagdhāḥ
śaileṣu śailā iva baddha mūlāḥ
verses.translation: "When the swarthy clouds full with new waters are docking among swarthily clouds, they are shining forth like mountains burnt by wildfire docking among other mountains that are already burnt by wildfire, both moored at mountain-bases.

glosses.meaning: by forest fire, burnt, among mountains
by forest fire, burnt, mountains, like

verses.devanagari:
प्रमत्त संनाददित बर्हिणानि
स शक्रगोप अकुल शाद्वलानि |
चरन्ति नीप अर्जुन वासितानि
गजाः सुरम्याणि वन अन्तराणि
verses.iast:
pramatta saṃnādadita bar.hhiṇāni
sa śakragopa akula śādvalāni |
caranti nīpa arjuna vāsitāni
gajāḥ suramyāṇi vana antarāṇi
verses.translation: "Elephants are moving about the very pleasant interiors of forests where peahens are voluptuously screaming, pasturelands are overspread with red-beetles, and where they are fragranced with the flowers of Niipa and Arjuna trees.

verses.devanagari:
नव अंबु धार आहत केसराणि
द्रुतम् परित्यज्य सरोरुहाणि |
कदंब पुष्पाणि स केसराणि
नवानि हृष्टा भ्रमराः पिबन्ति
verses.iast:
nava ambu dhāra āhata kesarāṇi
drutam parityajya saroruhāṇi |
kadamba puṣpāṇi sa kesarāṇi
navāni hṛṣṭā bhramarāḥ pibanti
verses.translation: "Lashed are the fibrils of lotuses with the downpour of new waters, hence quickly leaving them off the joyful honeybees are quaffing the Kadamba flowers with new fibrils.

glosses.meaning: with new, water, streams, lashed, fibrils

verses.devanagari:
मत्ता गजेन्द्रा मुदिता गवेन्द्रा
वनेषु विक्रांततरा मृगेन्द्राः |
रम्या नगेन्द्रा निभृता नरेन्द्राः
प्रक्रीडितो वारि धरैः सुरेन्द्रः
verses.iast:
mattā gajendrā muditā gavendrā
vaneṣu vikrāṃtatarā mṛgendrāḥ |
ramyā nagendrā nibhṛtā narendrāḥ
prakrīḍito vāri dharaiḥ surendraḥ
verses.translation: "In forests lordly elephants are ruttish, ideal bulls that are delighted, peerless lions are triumphant to a better degree, lofty mountains are heart-pleasant, lords of people are withdrawing from their campaigns, and the lord of gods, Indra, is playing well with water giving clouds.

glosses.meaning: of animals, lordly ones - lions, are triumphant, to a better degree

verses.devanagari:
मेघाः समुद् भूत समुद्र नादा
महाजल ओघैः गगन अवलंबाः |
नदीः तटाकानि सरांसि वापिः
महीम् च कृत्स्नाम् अपवाहयन्ति
verses.iast:
meghāḥ samud bhūta samudra nādā
mahājala oghaiḥ gagana avalambāḥ |
nadīḥ taṭākāni sarāṃsi vāpiḥ
mahīm ca kṛtsnām apavāhayanti
verses.translation: "The clouds having torrential water are soaring the sky, and spurning the booms of oceans with their rumbles they are inundating rivers, lakes, pools, tanks and even the earth.

glosses.meaning: verily, over, thrown - spurning, ocean's, boom

verses.devanagari:
वर्ष प्रवेगा विपुला पतन्ति
प्रवान्ति वाताः समुदीर्ण वेगाः |
प्रनष्ट कूलाः प्रवहन्ति शीघ्रम्
नद्यो जलम् विप्रतिपन्न मार्गाः
verses.iast:
varṣa pravegā vipulā patanti
pravānti vātāḥ samudīrṇa vegāḥ |
pranaṣṭa kūlāḥ pravahanti śīghram
nadyo jalam vipratipanna mārgāḥ
verses.translation: "Rains are falling substantially and speedily, gales are blowing intensified in their speediness, while rivers are conducting water speedily over their eroded riverbanks and far afield of their course.

glosses.meaning: intensified, in speediness, gales, are blowing
contradictory, having their course - out of ordinary course, far afield

verses.devanagari:
नरैः नरेन्द्रा इव पर्वतेन्द्राः
सुरेन्द्र नीतैः पवन उपनीतैः |
घन अंबु कुम्भैः अभिषिच्यमाना
रूपम् श्रियम् स्वाम् इव दर्शयन्ति
verses.iast:
naraiḥ narendrā iva par.hvatendrāḥ
surendra nītaiḥ pavana upanītaiḥ |
ghana ambu kumbhaiḥ abhiṣicyamānā
rūpam śriyam svām iva darśayanti
verses.translation: "Lords of people will be anointed by people with water carried in pots on their shoulders, and then those kings show their propitious aspect of a humanly king with applied divinity, whereas the lords of mountains are being anointed with the water sent directly by Indra and hitherto wafted straight by Air-god in the pots called black-clouds, thus these lordly mountains are standing alone as if showing their grandeur and divinity on earth.

glosses.meaning: gods, lord - by Indra, brought - sent

verses.devanagari:
घन उपगूढम् गगनम् न तारा
न भास्करो दर्शनम् अभ्युपैति |
नवैः जल ओघैः धरणी वितृप्ता
तमो विलिप्ता न दिशः प्रकाशाः
verses.iast:
ghana upagūḍham gaganam na tārā
na bhāskaro darśanam abhyupaiti |
navaiḥ jala oghaiḥ dharaṇī vitṛptā
tamo viliptā na diśaḥ prakāśāḥ
verses.translation: "Sky is closely enshrouded with clouds, neither sun nor stars are getting around for a glimpse, earth is fully satiated with the torrents of new water, enswathed in obscurity the precincts are unilluminated...
notes: The statement of 'obscurity and illumination' is suggestive of the Vedic import tamasomā jyotirgamaya 'from darkness lead me unto light...' When the earth itself is satisfied with the gift of nature the earthlings are still hankering after inaccessible desires, thus they cycle through the karmic cycle.

glosses.meaning: sky is, by clouds, closely, enshrouded
sun, to see, not, getting around - imperceivable

glosses.itrans: tamaH vi liptaa dishaH na prakaashaaH
glosses.iast: tamaḥ vi liptā diśaḥ na prakāśāḥ
glosses.devanagari: तमः वि लिप्ता दिशः न प्रकाशाः
glosses.meaning: by obscurity, verily, swathed, precincts, not, illuminated.

verses.devanagari:
महान्ति कूटानि मही धराणाम्
धारा विधौतानि अधिकम् विभान्ति |
महा प्रमाणैः विपुलैः प्रपातैः
मुक्त कलापैः इव लंबमानैः
verses.iast:
mahānti kūṭāni mahī dharāṇām
dhārā vidhautāni adhikam vibhānti |
mahā pramāṇaiḥ vipulaiḥ prapātaiḥ
muk{}ta kalāpaiḥ iva lambamānaiḥ
verses.translation: "The paramount pinnacles of the mountains are thoroughly washed by the torrential rains and are shining forth surpassingly, and the voluminous and widespread torrents that are pitching down are like the pearly necklaces pendulous on the chests of mountains.

glosses.meaning: by earth, born ones - of mountains
of large, volume - voluminous, widespread, that pitches down - torrential rains

verses.devanagari:
शैलोपल प्रस्खलमान वेगाः
शैलोत्तमानाम् विपुलाः प्रपाताः |
गुहासु संनादित बर्हिणासु
हारा विकीर्यन्त इव अवभान्ति
verses.iast:
śailopala praskhalamāna vegāḥ
śailottamānām vipulāḥ prapātāḥ |
guhāsu saṃnādita barhiṇāsu
hārā vikīryanta iva avabhānti
verses.translation: "Washing the mountain stones speedily the torrents on the lofty mountains are widespread and entering the caves, in which peacocks are highly screaming, and thus they are in the gleam of lavalieres strewn around.
notes: The mountain rapids are running helter-skelter on the mountain washing the boulders speedily. But the boulders according to their nature obstruct these rapids. When obstructed they have the only recourse to enter the nearest cave. The caves by then are already full with screaming and colourful peacocks. Adding to the lustre of those peacock's variegated colours, the pearly-white water has also entered the caves. Then these three, pearly water, colourful peacocks, blackish caves are giving out sparkles of their own, like necklaces studded with many colourful gems, and if many such pendants are strewn around, each of its studded stone emits its own colour.

glosses.meaning: on mountain, stones, verily, falling, speedily
that are with - highly screaming, peacocks

glosses.itrans: haaraa vi kiiryanta iva ava bhaanti
glosses.iast: hārā vi kīryanta iva ava bhānti
glosses.devanagari: हारा वि कीर्यन्त इव अव भान्ति
glosses.meaning: lavalieres, strewn around, like, well, gleaming.

verses.devanagari:
शीघ्र प्रवेगा विपुलाः प्रपाता
निर्धौत शृंग उपतला गिरीणाम् |
मुक्ता कलाप प्रतिमाः पतन्तो
महा गुह उस्त्संग तलैः ध्रियन्ते
verses.iast:
śīghra pravegā vipulāḥ prapātā
nir.hdhauta śṛṃga upatalā girīṇām |
muk{}tā kalāpa pratimāḥ patanto
mahā guha ustsaṃga talaiḥ dhriyante
verses.translation: "On neatly washing the crests of wide mountains and their nearby planes, the high-speeded waterfalls are falling like pearl-necklaces and the mountains are wearing them at the planes of their cavernous caves.
notes: The mountains are noblemen in simile. The mountain rapids are pearly-necklaces firstly falling around their necks, and then drooping onto their chests, thus culminating at their locket-position, i.e., at the caves, on the chest of mountains. Those caves are glittering with the colours of peacocks, pearly water and blackish caves. Thus the utsanga 'heart of hearts...' these noblemen's hearts of hearts are covered with such necklaces and lockets.

glosses.meaning: on neatly, washing, on crest of mountains, nearby, planes

verses.devanagari:
सुरताम् अर्द विच्छिन्नाः स्वर्ग स्त्री हार मौक्तिकाः |
पतन्ति च अतुलाः दिक्षु तोय धाराः समन्ततः
verses.iast:
suratām arda vicchinnāḥ svarga strī hāra mauk{}tikāḥ |
patanti ca atulāḥ dikśu toya dhārāḥ samantataḥ
verses.translation: "Like the strings of pearls of heavenly females plopping down when broken in the friction of lovemaking, excellent streams of water are falling all over and in all directions.

glosses.meaning: in lovemaking, in friction, broke apart

verses.devanagari:
विलीयमानैः विहगैः निमीलद्भिः च पंकजैः |
विकसन्त्या च मालत्या गतो अस्तम् ज्ञायते रविः
verses.iast:
vilīyamānaiḥ vihagaiḥ nimīladbhiḥ ca paṃkajaiḥ |
vikasantyā ca mālatyā gato astam jñāyate raviḥ
verses.translation: "With the return of birds to nests, doubling up of lotuses, and blooming up jasmines, the sun is know to have gone into dusk.

glosses.meaning: by crouching in - returning to nests, of birds
blooming up, of Jasmine flowers, also with
sun, into dusk, gone, known to be.

verses.devanagari:
वृत्ता यात्रा नरेन्द्राणाम् सेना पथि एव वर्तते |
वैराणि चैव मार्गाः च सलिलेन समीकृताः
verses.iast:
vṛttā yātrā narendrāṇām senā pathi eva var.htate |
vairāṇi caiva mārgāḥ ca salilena samīkṛtāḥ
verses.translation: "Reversed are the campaigns of kings as the armies are marooned and thus rainwater has neutralised conflicts and roadways.

glosses.meaning: people's, lords - of kings, campaigns, reversed
armies, on path, only, remaining - marooned

verses.devanagari:
मासि प्रौष्ठपदे ब्रह्म ब्राह्मणानाम् विवक्षताम् |
अयम् अध्याय समयः सामगानाम् उपस्थितः
verses.iast:
māsi prauṣṭhapade brahma brāhmaṇānām vivakṣatām |
ayam adhyāya samayaḥ sāmagānām upasthitaḥ
verses.translation: "The month of Bhaadrapada, August-September, is the time for learning the singing of Sama Veda, and this is the time that has come for those Brahmans who concern themselves for learning the singing of Sama Veda.
notes: During this time a vow called cātur māsya vrata will be observed by all adherers of Veda-s, and during this time young celibates are initiated into Vedic studies which commences on bhādrapada śukla tṛtīya 'third day in the white-fortnight of this Bhaadrapada month.'

verses.devanagari:
निवृत्त कर्म आयतनो नूनम् संचित संचयः |
आषाढीम् अभ्युपगतो भरतः कोसल अधिपः
verses.iast:
nivṛtta karma āyatano nūnam saṃcita saṃcayaḥ |
āṣāḍhīm abhyupagato bharataḥ kosala adhipaḥ
verses.translation: "On carrying out all the domestic affairs and completely garnering the goods for rainy season, Bharata, the king of Kosala, might have definitely undertaken the 'four-month-vow' on the full moon day of aSaaDha month.

glosses.meaning: one who has carried out, affairs, domestic
full moon day - pertaining to aaSaadha month

verses.devanagari:
नूनम् आपूर्यमाणायाः सरय्वा वधते रयः |
माम् समीक्ष्य समायान्तम् अयोध्याया इव स्वनः
verses.iast:
nūnam āpūryamāṇāyāḥ sarayvā vadhate rayaḥ |
mām samīkṣya samāyāntam ayodhyāyā iva svanaḥ
verses.translation: "Definitely the River Sarayu must be overfilling and its swashing must be mounting as with the commotion of Ayodhya on beholding my returning to city.
notes: Ayodhya and its people used to create hubbubs whenever Rama used to return to city after his short trips to outside. Such is the affection of the inmates of Ayodhya to Rama, and now Rama is reminiscing that hubbub of people and swashing of Sarayu, as both soundalike.

verses.devanagari:
इमाः स्फीत गुणा वर्षाः सुग्रीवः सुखम् अश्नुते |
विजित अरिः स दारः च राज्ये महति च स्थितः
verses.iast:
imāḥ sphīta guṇā varṣāḥ sugrīvaḥ sukham aśnute |
vijita ariḥ sa dāraḥ ca rājye mahati ca sthitaḥ
verses.translation: "This rainy season as such has manifold inbuilt facilities for self-contained entertainment, so Sugreeva must be luxuriating in them, besides, revelling for conquering his enemy, regaining his wife, and instituting himself as a king of an admirable kingdom.

glosses.meaning: one who has - verily, conquered, enemy - Sugreeva on conquering Vali
that have - manifold, merits - inbuilt facilities, these, rains - in rainy season
luxuries, he partakes - he luxuriate in.

verses.devanagari:
अहम् तु हृत दारः च राज्यात् च महतः च्युतः |
नदी कूलम् इव क्लिन्नम् अवसीदामि लक्ष्मण
verses.iast:
aham tu hṛta dāraḥ ca rājyāt ca mahataḥ cyutaḥ |
nadī kūlam iva klinnam avasīdāmi lakṣmaṇa
verses.translation: "As for me, Lakshmana, I am the one who is toppled from a great kingdom, whose wife is stolen, such as I am, I am toppling down like a riverbank that is toppled over.

glosses.meaning: from a great, kingdom, fallen - toppled from
I am, on my part - as for me
wetted - toppled over, river, bank, like

verses.devanagari:
शोकः च मम विस्तीर्णो वर्षाः च भृश दुर्गमाः |
रावणः च महान् शत्रुः अपारम् प्रतिभाति मे
verses.iast:
śokaḥ ca mama vistīrṇo varṣāḥ ca bhṛśa durgamāḥ |
rāvaṇaḥ ca mahān śatruḥ apāram pratibhāti me
verses.translation: "Also my anguish is boundless, the rains have definitely made the pathways impassable, my enemy Ravana is a formidable one, thus these three appear to me as insurmountable obstacles.

glosses.meaning: rains, also, definitely, not, passable - pathways are impassable
not, possible to cross over - not, negotiable - insurmountable obstacles

verses.devanagari:
अयात्राम् चैव दृष्ट्वा इमाम् मार्गाम् च भृश दुर्गमान् |
प्रणते चैव सुग्रीवे न मया किंचित् ईरितम्
verses.iast:
ayātrām caiva dṛṣṭvā imām mārgām ca bhṛśa durgamān |
praṇate caiva sugrīve na mayā kiñcit īritam
verses.translation: "Though Sugreeva is very humble to embark on a campaign, visualising the rainy season as an impossible one for any campaign, and even the pathways are rendered highly impassable I have not said anything to him in the affirmative.

glosses.meaning: Sugreeva is, very, humble, also thus

verses.devanagari:
अपि च अति परिक्लिष्टम् चिरात् दारैः समागतम् |
आत्म कार्य गरीयस्त्वात् वक्तुम् न इच्छामि वानरम्
verses.iast:
api ca ati parikliṣṭam cirāt dāraiḥ samāgatam |
ātma kārya garīyastvāt vak{}tum na icchāmi vānaram
verses.translation: "Even Sugreeva has undergone many difficulties in their entirety, after a long while he is united with his wife, and even owing to the magnitude involved in our task of tracking down Ravana I did not desire to insist on that monkey.

glosses.meaning: much, entirely, difficulties - that Sugreeva has undergone
after a long while, with wife, united with
our, work, owing to loftiness of due to magnitude involved in our task

verses.devanagari:
स्वयम् एव हि विश्रम्य ज्ञात्वा कालम् उपागतम् |
उपकारम् च सुग्रीवो वेत्स्यते न अत्र संशयः
verses.iast:
svayam eva hi viśramya jñātvā kālam upāgatam |
upakāram ca sugrīvo vetsyate na atra saṃśayaḥ
verses.translation: "After a respite Sugreeva will realise on his own that the time has come, and he will also realise the he has something to requite, isn't it! So, there needn't be any doubt in that matter.

glosses.meaning: time's, closely, coming in, on realising
on his own, thus, will know, isn't it
= in that, doubt, is not there.

verses.devanagari:
तस्मात् काल प्रतीक्षो अहम् स्थितो अस्मि शुभ लक्षण |
सुग्रीवस्य नदीनाम् च प्रसादम् अभिकांक्षयन्
verses.iast:
tasmāt kāla pratīkṣo aham sthito asmi śubha lakṣaṇa |
sugrīvasya nadīnām ca prasādam abhikāṃkśayan
verses.translation: "I therefore stay abidingly looking forward for the time, oh, Lakshmana with felicitous aspects, expectant of the generosity of Sugreeva and of these rivers.

glosses.meaning: oh, one with felicitous aspect, Lakshmana
abiding, time, looking forward to, I am.

verses.devanagari:
उपकारेण वीरो हि प्रतिकारेण युज्यते |
अकृतज्ञो अप्रतिकृतो हन्ति सत्त्ववताम् मनः
verses.iast:
upakāreṇa vīro hi pratikāreṇa yujyate |
akṛtajño apratikṛto hanti sattvavatām manaḥ
verses.translation: "A valiant one who is succoured will be indebted with some requital on his part, but besides being unfaithful, if one who does not make requital for all the favours done in his interest, he will be wounding the hearts of soft-hearted people." Rama said so to Lakshmana, keeping Sugreeva in view.

verses.devanagari:
अथ एवम् उक्तः प्रणिधाय लक्ष्मणः
कृत अंजलिः तत् प्रतिपूज्य भाषितम् |
उवाच रामम् स्वभिराम दर्शनम्
प्रदर्शयन् दर्शनम् आत्मनः शुभम्
verses.iast:
atha evam uk{}taḥ praṇidhāya lakṣmaṇaḥ
kṛta aṃjaliḥ tat pratipūjya bhāṣitam |
uvāca rāmam svabhirāma darśanam
pradarśayan darśanam ātmanaḥ śubham
verses.translation: Visualising what Rama said about their waiting for pre-winter season to be candid, and praisefully making palm-fold at that determination of Rama, and even to clarify his own opportune viewpoint, Lakshmana spoke to Rama who by his own aspect is a delightful one for a ken.

verses.devanagari:
यत् उक्तम् एतत् तव सर्वम् ईप्सितम्
नर इन्द्र कर्ता नचिरा हरि ईश्वरः |
शरत् प्रतीक्षः क्षमताम् इमम् भवान्
जल प्रपातम् रिपु निग्रहे धृतः
verses.iast:
yat uk{}tam etat tava sarvam īpsitam
nara indra kartā nacirā hari īśvaraḥ |
śarat pratīkṣaḥ kṣamatām imam bhavān
jala prapātam ripu nigrahe dhṛtaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, lord of people, Sugreeva will be effectuating everything you have desired and said, not later but soon, hence awaiting autumn you may please bear up these heavy rainfalls, besides bearing with the idea of disciplining the enemy." So said Lakshmana to Rama.
notes: The last three verses are a repeat of 45, 46, and 47th verses of Ch 27 of this Kishkindha kaanda. Many of the verses in this canto bear the blemish of interpolations.
